criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Clearly states the primary mission, the single-spacecraft choice with rationale, and likely users. Users are not explicitly separated into operator and customers, and the operator is only implied. Background is well referenced, though some sources are weak and a Wikipedia source appears in the body.

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Covers most required elements with STK access data and orbit figures. However, the launch narrative contradicts itself (piggyback versus dedicated Vega E), the ground-station logic conflicts with the Tasmanian site, the EOL section is truncated and unresolved, and STK files and hand calculations are not shown.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Has the required sections and headings. Figures and tables are inconsistently labelled, with no figure numbers or table captions. Sentences are truncated or garbled, the access table has a duplicated row, and references are incomplete (e.g. '[5] f.', '[10 d.') and include Wikipedia.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Contradictory launch approach: the satellite is said to piggyback on a pre-planned mission, yet it is then assigned a dedicated Vega E rocket.
Claims high pass frequency requires a polar ground station, but the chosen Tasmanian site (~42°S) is not polar; the justification is weak.
States RAAN initial value 27.33° indicates the launch facility location; RAAN is not a site location and this is incorrect.
STK access table lists row 15 as a duplicate of row 14 and the total of 8711.797 s excludes it, so the statistics are inconsistent.
Passive versus controlled disposal reasoning is confused; drag sail description is truncated and unfinished.
Claim that launch windows occur twice daily because latitude is below inclination is asserted without calculation.

overall: Solid design coverage with STK access data and a justified SSO orbit, but undermined by contradictions in launch and ground-station logic, a truncated EOL section, a duplicated access row, missing figure labels, and Wikipedia sourcing. Substantial revision is needed.

feedback.summary: You have a clear primary mission, a well-justified single-spacecraft choice, STK access data and a justified SSO orbit. The main gaps are contradictions in your launch and ground-station logic, an incorrect RAAN statement, and an unfinished end-of-life section. Your presentation also needs numbered figures and tables, a corrected access table and complete, scholarly references.

criteria.C1: Your introduction clearly states the primary mission and explains why a single spacecraft is used, supported by references. To reach the top level, state the operator and the customers separately, for example by naming the operating organisation and listing CSIRO and BOM as customers. Replace weaker sources, including the Wikipedia reference, with authoritative literature.
criteria.C2: Your design covers most required elements, including STK access data and a justified SSO orbit. However, the launch section contradicts itself (piggyback versus dedicated Vega E), and your polar-station argument conflicts with your Tasmanian site at about 42°S. The RAAN explanation is incorrect and the EOL section is unfinished. Support claims with STK files and hand calculations.
criteria.C3: You reach some sensible conclusions, including the launch-vehicle uncertainty for the Vega E. They are rather generic. Restate key results, such as your orbital elements, pass counts and end-of-life decision, and link each one back to the mission purpose.
criteria.C4: The report has the required sections and headings, but figures and tables lack numbers and captions, and some sentences are unfinished. The access table has a duplicated row, and some references are incomplete and include Wikipedia. Consistent labelling and complete, properly cited references would move your presentation towards the top level.

next_steps: Resolve the launch contradiction by choosing either rideshare on a pre-planned mission or a dedicated Vega E, and justify the choice. Support the twice-daily launch window claim with a calculation.

Correct the ground-station reasoning and the RAAN statement. Complete the EOL section with a clear choice between passive and controlled disposal, including the drag sail description. Remove the duplicated access row and recalculate the totals.

Label every figure and table with a number and caption. Add STK files and hand calculations to an appendix. Replace Wikipedia and incomplete references with scholarly sources, and restate key quantitative results in the conclusion.
